title: Just one selfie
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in the Emergency Department. You have just treated a well-known footballer for a minor ankle injury. As he gets ready to leave, he cheerfully offers to take a selfie with you.

Other patients are waiting nearby.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.brief: Friendly, and maintains a professional relationship.
options.detailed: Photos with patients, especially in a clinical area, can compromise confidentiality, including of other patients, and blur boundaries. A friendly refusal is appropriate.

options.text: Take the selfie and post it on your own social media.
options.brief: Breaches his confidentiality and professional standards.
options.detailed: Posting a photo with a patient discloses that he was treated, and is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Take the photo, but ask him not to post it.
options.brief: Still takes a personal photo with a patient in a clinical area.
options.detailed: This seems a compromise, but you can't control what happens to the photo, and other patients may be in the background.

options.text: Suggest he contacts the trust's communications team if he'd like a photo with staff.
options.brief: Redirects a request to the people who manage it.
options.detailed: Some trusts arrange photos with well-known visitors in suitable settings. Pointing him there is polite, though not necessary. It ranks second because declining is the main point.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you maintain professional boundaries when a well-known patient offers a friendly gesture.
explanation.keyDetails: He offered, cheerfully. You are in a clinical area with other patients. He is well known.
explanation.reasoning: [A] declines politely, and [D] redirects the request. [C] still takes a personal photo, and [B] also discloses his treatment publicly.
explanation.competing: Some would see [C] as harmless, but you can't control what happens to the photo once it's taken.

references.title: Using social media as a medical professional
references.note: Doctors' use of social media and photos with patients.
